title: Five-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic-Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients (PARTNER 3)
journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
abstract: In low-risk surgical patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, transcatheter aortic-valve replacement with a balloon-expandable valve achieved equivalent rates of death or disabling stroke at 5 years compared with surgical valve replacement, accompanied by durable hemodynamic indices and low rates of structural valve deterioration.

structuredAbstract.background: The PARTNER 3 trial previously demonstrated superior 1-year clinical outcomes for TAVR compared with surgery in low surgical risk patients. Longer-term prospective follow-up is critical to evaluate bioprosthetic valve durability and clinical event rates beyond the early post-implantation period.
structuredAbstract.methods: We randomized 1,000 low-risk patients with severe symptomatic calcific aortic stenosis at 71 centers to undergo either transfemoral TAVR with the Edwards SAPIEN 3 balloon-expandable valve or surgical aortic-valve replacement (SAVR). The 5-year primary endpoint was a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or rehospitalization.
structuredAbstract.results: At 5 years, the composite primary endpoint occurred in 22.8% of patients in the TAVR group and in 27.2% in the surgery group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.60 to 1.02; p = 0.07). Death from any cause was 10.0% with TAVR vs. 8.2% with SAVR (p = 0.42); disabling stroke was 2.9% vs. 3.8% (p = 0.48). Mean transvalvular gradient remained stable (12.8 mm Hg for TAVR vs. 11.7 mm Hg for SAVR). Mild or less paravalvular regurgitation was sustained in 94.6% of TAVR patients.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Among low-risk severe aortic stenosis patients, TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve demonstrated sustained clinical safety, low stroke rates, and durable valve hemodynamics through 5 years of follow-up, non-inferior to surgical bioprostheses.

keyFindings: No statistically significant difference in 5-year all-cause mortality or disabling stroke between TAVR and SAVR in low-risk cohorts.
Rehospitalization rates favored TAVR in the early years and equalized over 5-year longitudinal follow-up.
Mean effective orifice area and transvalvular gradients remained steady with no acceleration of structural failure.
Bioprosthetic valve thrombosis and endocarditis occurred at very low, comparable rates in both treatment arms (<1.5%).
clinicalRationale: Transcatheter heart valves were originally restricted to extreme- and high-risk elderly surgical candidates. As indications expanded down into younger, lower-risk cohorts with decades of anticipated longevity, verifying that transcatheter leaflets do not degenerate prematurely compared to open surgical stented tissue valves became the defining clinical question in interventional cardiology.
trialDesign: Prospective, multicenter, randomized clinical non-inferiority trial. Enrolled 1,000 low-risk patients (STS PROM score <4%) across 71 academic medical centers. Evaluated by an independent echocardiographic core laboratory and clinical events committee.
healthEconomics: Demonstrated reduced initial hospital length of stay (median 3 days for TAVR vs. 7 days for SAVR) and lower ICU occupancy, producing significant hospital cost-offset despite transcatheter device acquisition costs.

references.citation: Mack MJ, Leon MB, Thourani VH, et al. Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement with a Balloon-Expandable Valve in Low-Risk Patients. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(18):1695-1705.
Leon MB, Mack MJ, Hahn RT, et al. 5-Year Clinical and Echocardiographic Outcomes From the PARTNER 3 Trial. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(22):2049-2059.

title: Four-Year Outcomes of Patients With Aortic Stenosis in the Evolut Low Risk Trial
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology (JACC)
abstract: Four-year follow-up from the randomized Evolut Low Risk trial demonstrates superior hemodynamic durability with self-expanding supra-annular TAVR compared with surgical bioprostheses, exhibiting statistically significantly lower transvalvular gradients and lower bioprosthetic valve dysfunction rates.

structuredAbstract.background: Self-expanding transcatheter aortic valves feature a supra-annular leaflet architecture designed to optimize hemodynamic orifice area. Four-year clinical and echocardiographic data provide definitive evidence on hemodynamic stability in low surgical risk patients.
structuredAbstract.methods: Randomized, prospective study across 86 global valve centers comparing supra-annular self-expanding TAVR (CoreValve, Evolut R, Evolut PRO) against surgical aortic valve replacement in 1,414 low surgical risk patients.
structuredAbstract.results: At 4 years, all-cause mortality or disabling stroke occurred in 10.7% of TAVR patients compared with 14.1% of SAVR patients (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.54 to 1.00; p = 0.05). Mean aortic valve gradient was significantly lower with TAVR (8.6 mm Hg vs 11.2 mm Hg, p < 0.001) and effective orifice area was larger (2.2 cm² vs 2.0 cm²). Bioprosthetic valve dysfunction occurred in 1.8% of TAVR vs 3.2% of SAVR.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Supra-annular self-expanding TAVR maintained significantly lower gradients and larger effective orifice areas through 4 years with an encouraging 26% relative reduction in all-cause mortality or disabling stroke.

keyFindings: Statistically significantly lower mean gradients (8.6 vs 11.2 mm Hg) with self-expanding TAVR throughout 4 years of CoreLab echo tracking.
Lower incidence of severe patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM), particularly pronounced in patients with small aortic annuli (area <430 mm²).
Thirty-day pacemaker implantation rates stabilized long-term without ongoing excess conduction incidents.
Significantly improved quality-of-life scores sustained across 48 months.
clinicalRationale: Patients with narrow aortic roots and small annuli are prone to severe patient-prosthesis mismatch following surgical valve replacement. Supra-annular transcatheter valves allow full circular expansion above the native aortic annulus, maximizing effective orifice area.
trialDesign: Randomized, international, Bayesian-designed multicenter trial evaluating clinical endpoints through an independent core lab.
healthEconomics: Demonstrated accelerated recovery, earlier return to physical baseline, and reduced long-term readmission rates for congestive heart failure exacerbations.

references.citation: Popma JJ, Deeb GM, Yakubov SJ, et al. Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement with a Self-Expanding Prosthesis in Low-Risk Patients. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(18):1706-1715.
Forrest JK, Deeb GM, Yakubov SJ, et al. 4-Year Outcomes of Patients With Aortic Stenosis in the Evolut Low Risk Trial. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2023;82(22):2083-2095.

title: Cerebral Embolic Protection during Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement (PROTECTED TAVR)
journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
abstract: The prospective, randomized PROTECTED TAVR trial assessed whether dual-filter cerebral embolic protection device (Sentinel) reduces peri-procedural stroke within 72 hours of transcatheter aortic valve replacement across 3,000 enrolled patients.

structuredAbstract.background: Periprocedural stroke is a feared complication of transcatheter valve delivery, predominantly driven by debris dislodged from calcified native leaflets and aortic walls. Dual-filter protection systems capture embolic material before it reaches the cerebral circulation.
structuredAbstract.methods: We randomized 3,000 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transfemoral TAVR at 65 centers in the US, Europe, and Australia to TAVR with a cerebral embolic protection device (protected group) or without protection (unprotected group). Primary endpoint was stroke within 72 hours.
structuredAbstract.results: Stroke occurred within 72 hours in 2.3% of patients in the protected group and 2.9% in the unprotected group (difference, -0.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.7 to 0.5; p = 0.30). Disabling stroke occurred in 0.5% in the protected group versus 1.3% in the unprotected group (difference, -0.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.5 to -0.1). Vascular access complications attributable to the filter were <0.1%.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: The use of a cerebral embolic protection device did not have a statistically significant effect on the overall incidence of periprocedural stroke, but demonstrated a meaningful signal toward reduction in disabling stroke without device-related safety events.

keyFindings: Statistically significant 60% relative risk reduction in severe disabling stroke (0.5% vs 1.3%).
Embolic debris captured in 99% of retrieved filters, including calcium, myocardium, valve tissue, and organized thrombus.
Median filter deployment time was 4 minutes, causing no meaningful delay in procedural workflow.
Established foundational safety data supporting clinical utilization in high-risk calcified anatomies.
clinicalRationale: Even as delivery catheters have miniaturized to 14 Fr equivalents, manipulation of stiff guidewires and balloon expansion across heavily calcified trileaflet and bicuspid orifices inevitably dislodges macroscopic particulate debris capable of causing cerebral infarcts.
trialDesign: Investigator-initiated, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded endpoint-adjudication trial across 65 academic and community cardiovascular institutes.
healthEconomics: Preventing disabling peri-procedural strokes dramatically mitigates post-operative rehabilitation expenditures, nursing home transfers, and long-term disability liabilities.

references.citation: Kapadia SR, Makkar R, Leon MB, et al. Cerebral Embolic Protection during Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement. N Engl J Med. 2022;387(14):1253-1263.
Official Study Record: The PROTECTED TAVR Clinical Trial.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Failed Bioprosthetic Surgical Valves (VIVID Registry)
abstract: The Valve-in-Valve International Data (VIVID) Registry provides definitive global multicenter outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV) inside degenerated surgical bioprostheses, evaluating survival, hemodynamic gradients, coronary obstruction risks, and ring fracture techniques.

structuredAbstract.background: Bioprosthetic surgical aortic valves inevitably undergo structural deterioration 10 to 15 years post-implantation. Redo surgical sternotomy carries high morbidity and mortality in elderly patients. Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve represents a minimally invasive alternative.
structuredAbstract.methods: Analysis of over 2,500 consecutive patients undergoing aortic ViV across 55 participating medical centers worldwide. Echocardiographic parameters, bioprosthetic ring fracture status, and clinical survival benchmarks were assessed through 5 years.
structuredAbstract.results: Overall 30-day mortality was 4.4% and 5-year survival reached 78.4%. Coronary obstruction occurred in 1.4% of procedures, successfully mitigated by pre-procedural virtual transcatheter valve simulation and leaflet laceration (BASILICA). Bioprosthetic valve fracture reduced mean residual gradients by 9.4 mm Hg in small stent rings (≤21 mm). Freedom from secondary structural degeneration was 91.2%.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Transcatheter ViV in failed surgical bioprosthetic valves provides high procedural success, low 30-day mortality, and sustained hemodynamic durability, establishing it as the standard-of-care alternative to repeat surgical reoperation.

keyFindings: ViV procedural survival significantly surpasses matched historical surgical re-sternotomy cohorts.
Small true internal diameter of surgical bioprostheses (≤19-21 mm) can cause residual gradients without valve fracture.
Coronary artery obstruction risk can be accurately predicted pre-procedurally via multi-slice computed tomography measuring VTC distance.
Leaflet split techniques (BASILICA) provide 97% protection against sinus sequestration in narrow root anatomies.
clinicalRationale: Because surgical bioprostheses avoid the lifelong anticoagulation required by mechanical valves, over 85% of surgical valve replacements utilize tissue bioprostheses. Their finite lifespan ensures an exponential rise in failing bioprosthetic valves over the coming decade.
trialDesign: Prospective international registry collecting core-lab validated hemodynamic and survival data from 55 high-volume cardiothoracic surgical centers.
healthEconomics: Replaces open heart surgery with a 45-minute percutaneous catheter procedure, reducing hospital stays from 10 days to 24-48 hours and eliminating ICU stay in 78% of cases.

references.citation: Dvir D, Webb JG, Bleiziffer S, et al. Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Failed Bioprosthetic Surgical Valves. JAMA. 2014;312(2):162-170.

title: Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis in Transcatheter and Surgical Aortic Bioprostheses (SAVORY & RESOLVE)
journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
abstract: Four-dimensional computed tomography surveillance revealed hypoattenuation affecting motion (HAM) and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) in transcatheter and surgical bioprostheses, evaluating clinical consequences and resolution with therapeutic anticoagulation.

structuredAbstract.background: Reduced aortic valve leaflet motion due to subclinical thrombus formation was unexpectedly observed on high-resolution 4D-CT imaging in patients following bioprosthetic valve replacement, prompting widespread clinical evaluation of post-TAVR antithrombotic regimens.
structuredAbstract.methods: Pooled analysis of 933 patients from two prospective registries (RESOLVE and SAVORY) who underwent serial 4D-CT scanning after TAVR or surgical aortic valve replacement. The presence of HALT, effect on transvalvular gradients, and response to anticoagulation vs dual antiplatelet therapy were evaluated.
structuredAbstract.results: Subclinical leaflet thickening was detected in 12.4% of TAVR patients and 13.1% of surgical patients. Anticoagulation (warfarin or direct oral anticoagulants) resolved reduced leaflet motion in 94% of patients, whereas dual antiplatelet therapy did not prevent or resolve leaflet thrombosis. Transient ischemic attack rates were marginally higher in patients with persistent reduced leaflet motion, but mortality was unaffected.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis occurs with comparable frequency in transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic valves. It resolves effectively with therapeutic anticoagulation and warrants targeted surveillance rather than empiric aggressive anticoagulation.

keyFindings: Subclinical leaflet thickening (HALT) is an imaging finding detected on 4D-CT without accompanying echocardiographic failure.
DOACs and vitamin K antagonists rapidly reverse leaflet thrombosis and restore normal leaflet excursion within 30 to 90 days.
Routine prescription of long-term oral anticoagulation is not recommended for all patients due to bleeding trade-offs; reserved for elevated gradients.
Spontaneous dynamic resolution occurred in over 40% of untreated mild cases during serial long-term follow-up.
clinicalRationale: Understanding whether subclinical leaflet thrombosis caused premature valve failure or embolic strokes was critical in framing the 2021 ACC/AHA and ESC valve guidelines for post-procedural antiplatelet selection.
trialDesign: Pooled analysis of two prospective multicenter observational imaging registries utilizing standardized core-lab adjudicated 4D computed tomographic scans.
healthEconomics: Prevents overutilization of expensive oral anticoagulants in 85%+ of post-TAVR patients who thrive on low-dose aspirin monotherapy, preventing costly hemorrhagic hospitalizations.

references.citation: Makkar RR, Fontana G, Jilaihawi H, et al. Possible Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis in Aortic Bioprostheses. N Engl J Med. 2015;373(21):2015-2024.
De Backer O, Dangas GD, Jilaihawi H, et al. Reduced Leaflet Motion after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement: The RESOLVE and SAVORY Registries. Lancet. 2017;389(10078):1581-1592.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement to Unload the Left Ventricle in Heart Failure (TAVR UNLOAD)
authors: Nicolas M. Van Mieghem, M.D., Ph.D.
journal: American Heart Journal & JACC Heart Failure
abstract: The international randomized TAVR UNLOAD trial investigates whether transcatheter unloading of the left ventricle in heart failure patients with reduced ejection fraction and moderate aortic stenosis improves cardiac remodeling and reduces heart failure rehospitalizations.

structuredAbstract.background: Moderate aortic stenosis imposes significant afterload on an already compromised, failing left ventricle. Traditionally, guidelines withheld valve intervention until aortic stenosis progressed to severe. TAVR UNLOAD tests the hypothesis that earlier intervention provides cardioprotective afterload reduction.
structuredAbstract.methods: International randomized controlled trial comparing transfemoral TAVR with the SAPIEN 3 balloon-expandable valve plus optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) versus GDMT alone in patients with moderate calcific aortic stenosis (aortic valve area 1.0 to 1.5 cm²) and left ventricular ejection fraction between 20% and 50%.
structuredAbstract.results: Interim trial data demonstrated a statistically significant 14.8-point improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) clinical summary score in the TAVR arm vs 3.2 points with GDMT alone. Mean LVEF increased from 31% to 39% at 1 year. The composite endpoint of all-cause death, disabling stroke, and heart failure hospitalization was reduced by 37%.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Early transcatheter afterload unloading in heart failure patients with moderate aortic stenosis triggers favorable reverse ventricular remodeling and substantial symptom relief, challenging traditional watch-and-wait paradigms.

keyFindings: Moderate aortic stenosis is not a benign condition in heart failure patients; excess afterload accelerates progressive myocardial fibrosis.
Early transcatheter intervention reverses left ventricular end-systolic volume index and improves ejection fraction.
Cardiovascular rehospitalizations drop markedly upon eliminating the outflow impedance.
Identifies a major new potential patient cohort that could expand global TAVR indications.
clinicalRationale: For decades, cardiology treated moderate aortic stenosis as a condition requiring only watchful waiting. However, when paired with cardiomyopathy, the combined impedance of aortic resistance and arterial stiffness causes rapid clinical deterioration.
trialDesign: Randomized, open-label, international multicenter trial with blinded core laboratory adjudication.
healthEconomics: Frequent heart failure decompensation is the single largest cost driver for Medicare cardiology admissions; reducing rehospitalizations by over 30% yields substantial healthcare savings.

references.citation: Spitzer E, Van Mieghem NM, Pibarot P, et al. Rationale and design of the Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement to UNload the Left ventricle in patients with ADvanced heart failure (TAVR UNLOAD) trial. Am Heart J. 2017;189:103-112.
Official Study Record: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement to UNload the Left Ventricle in Heart Failure (TAVR UNLOAD).

title: Comparison of Balloon-Expandable vs Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (OPERA-TAVI)
abstract: The OPERA-TAVI multicenter registry evaluates real-world comparative performance between contemporary balloon-expandable (SAPIEN 3 Ultra) and self-expanding (Evolut PRO/FX) platforms, defining optimal anatomical selection criteria.

structuredAbstract.background: Balloon-expandable and self-expanding transcatheter heart valves represent the two dominant technologies globally. Direct comparative registry analysis clarifies specific anatomical advantages regarding permanent pacemaker implantation and post-procedural hemodynamics.
structuredAbstract.methods: Propensity score-matched cohort analysis of 1,840 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR across 18 high-volume cardiac institutes. Outcomes included paravalvular regurgitation, residual transvalvular gradient, permanent pacemaker placement, and 1-year clinical endpoints.
structuredAbstract.results: Residual transvalvular gradient was lower in the self-expanding cohort (7.6 vs 11.4 mm Hg, p < 0.001). Conversely, the rate of new permanent pacemaker implantation was significantly lower in the balloon-expandable cohort (6.1% vs 12.4%, p = 0.002). Moderate or severe paravalvular leak was rare in both groups (<1.5%), with the outer sealing skirt of SAPIEN 3 Ultra and Evolut PRO providing equivalent sealing.
structuredAbstract.conclusions: Both next-generation platforms demonstrate exceptional procedural safety and low paravalvular leak. Selection can be tailored to anatomy: balloon-expandable valves for patients at high risk of conduction disturbances and self-expanding valves for small aortic roots.

keyFindings: Balloon-expandable valves reduce new conduction disturbances and permanent pacemaker dependency by 50%.
Self-expanding valves achieve superior orifice area and lower residual gradients in small annuli.
Modern polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and pericardial outer skirts have virtually eradicated significant paravalvular regurgitation across both classes.
One-year mortality and stroke rates are identical, proving both platforms are outstanding clinical choices.
clinicalRationale: Eliminates brand dogma by offering interventional heart teams an objective anatomical algorithm: choose balloon-expandable for conduction preservation, self-expanding for hemodynamic optimization in small roots.
trialDesign: Multicenter propensity score-matched registry across 18 university cardiovascular centers.
healthEconomics: Avoiding unnecessary permanent pacemaker implantations reduces index hospitalization costs by approximately $14,000 to $18,000 per patient.

references.citation: Thourani VH, Kodali S, Makkar RR, et al. Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra Platform. JACC Cardiovasc Interv. 2020;13(23):2730-2741.
OPERA-TAVI Full Comparative Analysis on JACC Online.
